text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ontario hospitals plan for possible strike: Doctors' walkout would curtail emergency care, could send some patients out of the province.

- Federal voting may be staggered: Change in hours aimed at West. Voters in British Columbia will no longer cast their ballots knowing that the rest of the country has probably already elected a government if changes now being considered are accepted.
- Two Koreas play spy game in deadly earnest: North calls sub landing an accident as South hunts down survivors.
- Glitches in system keep payments in bank: Child-support money piling up in government account, Ontario Members of Provincial Parliament charge.
- Canadian Auto Workers union targets General Motors in hard-line bargaining: Long strike against auto maker could cost 3,500 jobs, deal blow to economy.
- Toronto Stock Exchange smashes volume record: Trading value mark on verge of being broken; stock frenzy brings windfall for brokerages.
- Churchill Falls power uproar may be linked to Voisey's Bay nickel deposit: Inco needs power for nickel smelter.
- Ultramar Corp joins U.S. firm to create oil giant: Merger with Diamond Shamrock Inc to product C$2.3-billion independent.
- Corel Corp launches attack on corporate market: Software pricing to challenge Microsoft.

- Oilpatch draws big money: Higher oil prices have put Canada's energy sector on track for a record C$7-billion in new financings this year. By the end of August C$5.7 billion had already been raised.
- Midland Walwyn sets up merchant bank. Midland announced it had created MWI & Partners, which will focus on investing in North American mid-market companies.
